title: A Deadline for the Extraction
premise: Oscar Voss, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471, works off-book cases that governments refuse to claim. When a safe house tied to her last investigation is listed for sale online — with interior photos revealing documents she buried years ago — she realizes someone is baiting her into the open. Pursued by an assassin who knows her routines better than her handlers do, Oscar races to expose a transnational cover-up that reaches into three governments and explains row twelve. In the end, she trades her own anonymity for the truth, publishing the files at devastating personal cost and finding, at last, a fragile sense of belonging among the few who believe her.
about_author: Rafael Halloran is a former aviation insurance adjuster who spent a decade reading wreckage reports before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town in Maine, where he claims every neighbor has a story they've sworn him to secrecy over.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Oscar Voss closes out another unattributable crash case in Lisbon, her POV establishing her methodical detachment and the ritual visit she pays to a memorial wall. A colleague mentions the anniversary of Flight 4471. Emotional beat: grief held under professional ice.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., Oscar finds the Marbella safe house for sale — with photos showing her own hidden document cache intact on the shelves. POV alternates briefly to the assassin, Marek, watching her building. Emotional beat: cold recognition that the trap is personal.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts her handler, Ilse Brandt, who denies authorizing the listing but slips a detail only insiders would know. Flashback to the night Oscar hid the files after 4471. Emotional beat: trust beginning to fracture inside her own agency.

chapters.title: Interior Photos
chapters.summary: Oscar studies the listing photos forensically, realizing one frame shows a reflection of the photographer — a man wearing Marek's distinctive ring. She understands she's being lured south. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Handler's Lie
chapters.summary: Ilse offers Oscar a desk job and a transfer; Oscar refuses and goes dark, copying her case archive first. A second POV thread opens: a Spanish intelligence officer, Rueda, who also recognizes the house. Emotional beat: crossing the line from investigator to fugitive.

chapters.title: Marbella
chapters.summary: Oscar reaches the safe house ahead of the sale viewing, retrieves the cache, and finds it tampered with — one file replaced by a photograph of row twelve taken from outside the aircraft. Emotional beat: the past reaching through the walls to touch her.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: During the scheduled open-house viewing, Oscar poses as a buyer among real estate agents while Marek circles the property. Rueda appears unexpectedly, claiming he was sent by a source inside the conspiracy. Emotional beat: paranoia — everyone could be the trap.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Rueda reveals a fragment: Flight 4471 carried a defector whose testimony three governments buried, and the crash was arranged. He wants Oscar's cache to complete his own case. Emotional beat: hope arriving wrapped in suspicion.

chapters.title: What Marek Knows
chapters.summary: Marek's POV chapter: we learn he was the failed extraction operative on 4471, that his failure killed the defector, and that his employers now want the loose ends — including Oscar — removed. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as another man owned by the machine.

chapters.title: Safe House Burning
chapters.summary: Marek torches the property with Oscar and Rueda barely escaping through the wine cellar; the document cache partially burns. They salvage a ledger naming a Brussels fixer. Emotional beat: loss, adrenaline, and the first true alliance between strangers.

chapters.title: Brussels Ledger
chapters.summary: In Brussels, Oscar decodes the ledger's payment routes, finding her own agency's shell company among the recipients. Ilse's name appears twice. Emotional beat: betrayal landing harder than any physical blow.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Rueda lays out the political geometry: Spain wants silence, France wants the defector discredited posthumously, and Oscar's own service wants the file closed. Any public move triggers all three. Emotional beat: the scale of the wall they must climb.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Oscar risks a dead-drop contact with Ilse, who confesses she signed off on burying 4471 to protect a ceasefire deal — but insists she never sanctioned the assassination order. Someone above her did. Emotional beat: a traitor who is also, in her way, a prisoner.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Contract
chapters.summary: Marek receives a revised contract: kill Oscar, Rueda, and Ilse, and stage it as domestic terrorism. His hesitation marks the first crack in his obedience. Emotional beat: the hunter questioning the hand that feeds him.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Oscar and Rueda attempt to courier copies to a journalist in The Hague; the courier is intercepted, and the journalist's office is raided hours later. They realize there's a leak inside Rueda's chain. Emotional beat: despair closing in from all sides.

chapters.title: Row Twelve, Reopened
chapters.summary: Oscar finally reads the recovered passenger manifest against the ledger and proves the defector survived the initial impact — meaning someone finished the job on the ground. Her family died as witnesses. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Ilse's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilse delivers the internal authorization trail to Oscar, knowing it ends her career and likely her life. Marek is dispatched to intercept them. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: At a Rotterdam freight yard, Marek corners them; instead of firing, he demands the truth about his own failed extraction be included in the record. An uneasy truce forms around shared guilt. Emotional beat: enemies discovering they were used by the same hands.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: The conspiracy moves to destroy the physical evidence — the 4471 wreckage storage facility — within forty-eight hours. Oscar, Rueda, Marek, and Ilse plan a simultaneous release across three jurisdictions so no single government can suppress it. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a weapon turned back on the hunters.

chapters.title: Wreckage
chapters.summary: Climax at the storage hangar: Marek holds off the cleanup team while Oscar photographs and streams the serial-numbered evidence; Ilse is fatally wounded buying them minutes. Rueda's leak is exposed and neutralized. Emotional beat: everything paid for at once.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: The files go live simultaneously in Madrid, Paris, and via the Hague journalist; inquiries open, resignations cascade, and Marek surrenders himself as the state's witness. Oscar watches her family's names enter the official record at last. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfect, late, and real.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Months later, Oscar testifies, declines reinstatement, and takes quiet work teaching crash reconstruction. She visits row twelve's memorial no longer as a mourner but as a witness, and lets two people — Rueda and the journalist — close enough to call friends. Emotional beat: memory honored, loneliness ended.
